name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add an always-visible, high-contrast focus ring to every interactive element. This guarantees keyboard users can see where they are at a glance, which is critical for people who rely on tabbing through pages. The trade-off is a slight visual clutter for sighted mouse users, but that’s minor compared to the accessibility win.

name: Reader
text: The always-visible ring overloads sighted keyboard users—cognitive noise rises with long lists, and the 250 ms delay risks dropping the ring entirely for users tabbing at 125 ms. Instead, show the ring only after a 100 ms pause on focus, then hide it after 2 seconds of inactivity. Test with Playwright MCP: measure time-to-target for keyboard users at 125 ms tab speed and track sighted users’ task completion time with/without the ring.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a single, high-contrast focus ring that appears immediately on key navigation and stays until another element is focused. This ensures keyboard users never lose their place, which is critical for efficiency and frustration reduction. The trade-off is a slight visual noise for sighted mouse users, but that’s minor compared to the accessibility win. Testing with Playwright will confirm the ring doesn’t interfere with rapid tabbing or reduced-motion preferences.

name: Reader
text: The always-visible ring creates real fatigue for sighted keyboard users in long forms—cognitive noise isn’t minor when every tab stop screams for attention. A better alternative: show the ring only after a 100 ms pause on focus, then hide it after 2 seconds of inactivity. Settle it with Playwright tests measuring both keyboard efficiency and user-reported distraction in a 20-item form.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Ship a **high-contrast focus ring with a 125ms delay**, toggleable via keyboard shortcut, validated with Playwright tests. Owned by Ramp.
